slides.title: Context Anxiety
slides.message: Finite windows + long sessions = agents rush or crash
slides.visual: bar chart: context usage growing over turns until threshold
slides.notes: Claude Code calls this the 'context anxiety' problem
slides.presenter_script: Every conversation eats context. Without compaction, agents either crash or rush to finish before running out.
slides.common_misconception: Bigger context windows solve this permanently
slides.transition: How do we compact without losing information?

slides.title: Three-Layer Pipeline
slides.message: Lossless prune → Structured distill → Lossy summarize
slides.visual: mermaid: flowchart showing three layers with budget checks between each
slides.notes: Each layer checks budget before escalating to the next
slides.presenter_script: The key principle: lossless before lossy. Remove duplicates first, truncate second, summarize last.
slides.common_misconception: Just summarize everything with the LLM

slides.title: Circuit Breaker
slides.message: Max 3 compaction cycles. If still over budget, stop and warn.
slides.visual: state diagram: compact → check → compact → check → TRIP
slides.notes: Prevents burning tokens on infinite summarization loops
slides.presenter_script: The circuit breaker prevents compaction from becoming more expensive than the conversation itself.
slides.common_misconception: Compaction always succeeds in reducing to target

slides.title: Chat Commands
slides.visual: terminal showing command examples and their effects
slides.notes: /compact forces all three layers; /clear keeps only system messages
slides.presenter_script: Users aren't helpless. Four slash-commands give direct control over context, sessions, and orientation.
